content.intro: In this lesson, you will explore xml naming rules within XML Syntax and Document Structure. You will connect its syllabus topics to an inspectable example, check the expected result, and note tool/version limits.
content.why_it_matters: XML Naming Rules matters because XML workflows rely on explicit structure and predictable processing. The lesson helps you reason about legal element names, avoid a common misunderstanding, and make a result reproducible for another developer.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson focuses on xml naming rules and the listed concepts: Legal element names; Legal attribute names; Name-start and name-character rules; Reserved naming conventions. XML processors enforce the syntax rules, while validation and application code can impose additional constraints.

content_blocks.title: Connect the subtopics
content_blocks.text: This lesson explicitly covers: Legal element names; Legal attribute names; Name-start and name-character rules; Reserved naming conventions; Creating meaningful names. Treat these as connected parts of one workflow: define the structure, make the relevant assumptions explicit, and verify a result with a small known input.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming a document is correct because it looks readable.
common_mistakes.why: Visual appearance does not prove well-formedness, schema validity, correct namespace handling, or application-level meaning.
common_mistakes.fix: Parse and validate the document with the intended processor, then assert its meaning using a focused test.

common_mistakes.problem: Mixing specification features with processor support.
common_mistakes.why: A standard may define features that a specific runtime does not implement.
common_mistakes.fix: Record the version and feature support; test with the actual target processor.

common_mistakes.why: Missing values, wrong types, namespace differences, or boundary inputs can expose failures.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a valid case, an invalid case, and an edge case to the verification notes.
